c74object.name: bachmcp.python
c74object.digest: Run a Python script in its own process and call its functions
c74object.description:
Runs a Python script in a process of its own, with arguments, and calls its functions while it runs. Max never waits for the script: a slow, hung or crashing script cannot freeze or crash Max. No shell is involved: each argument reaches the script's sys.argv as typed.
Nothing is preset: the object knows no Python and no working folder until you give them. run refuses until python and folder are set. Both take absolute paths, ~/..., Max paths (Macintosh HD:/...) or paths relative to the patch's own folder (the patch must be saved).
Calls and messages travel on a channel of their own (JSON lines on two pipes), never mixed with what the script prints: types survive both ways, and print() is only a log. A Python helper for it is the small bachmcp_max.py module: put it next to the script, which then imports it. Deleting the object or closing the patch stops the script and everything it started.

inlet.digest: run, call, eof, stop, kill, folder, python

outlet.digest: Messages from the script: out() and returned values

method.name: run
method.description: Starts <python> -u <script> <arguments...> with folder as its current directory. A relative script is found from folder. The arguments reach sys.argv one by one as typed (-a, --name, 3.5...); numbers as Max shows them. Max reads the arguments of a message box before they arrive, so put an argument with spaces in quotes. Sends pid <n> out of the right outlet when it starts and done <exit code> when it ends; error <reason> if python or folder is not set, or the folder, the script or Python is not found. One run at a time: a run while running is refused (send stop first). The script's stdin is empty: input() gets end of file instead of waiting forever.

method.name: call
method.digest: Call a function of the running script
method.description: Calls the function registered under that name with bachmcp_max's @on. Ints, floats and symbols arrive as int, float and str (a symbol 3 stays the str "3", a symbol with spaces is one str); the pair dictionary <name> among the arguments arrives as a dict. What the function returns leaves the left outlet with the function's name in front: None sends nothing, a list or tuple several atoms, a dict dictionary <name>. An unknown function, wrong arguments or an exception send failed <function> <message> out of the right outlet and the traceback to the log; the script goes on. Calls are answered in order. Max never waits: if the script is busy, calls are queued until it reads them. Refused (error) when nothing is running, or after eof.

method.name: eof
method.description: Closes the channel into the script once the calls already sent are written. bachmcp_max.loop() returns, so a script built around it ends and sends done.

method.name: stop
method.description: Sends Ctrl-C (SIGINT), which Python raises as KeyboardInterrupt, so the script can clean up. Still running 2 seconds later: SIGTERM; 2 seconds more: SIGKILL. Processes the script started are stopped too.

method.name: kill
method.description: SIGKILL to the script and the processes it started, without waiting.

attribute.name: python
attribute.description: The Python that runs the scripts: the file itself, for example /opt/homebrew/bin/python3, a venv's .venv/bin/python or a conda environment's bin/python. Max does not have your terminal's PATH, so a bare python is not looked up. No default: run refuses until it is set. A relative path starts from the patch's folder. python with no argument unsets it.

attribute.name: folder
attribute.description: The script's current directory, and where relative script paths start. No default: run refuses until it is set. A relative path starts from the patch's folder. folder with no argument unsets it.

attribute.name: console
attribute.digest: Print the log to the Max console
attribute.description: 1 (default): what the script prints is also printed to the Max console, stdout as posts and stderr (errors, tracebacks, warnings) as errors. 0: only out of the middle outlet.

attribute.name: label
attribute.value: Print stdout and stderr to the Console

entry.name: Messages (left outlet)
entry.description: Only what the script sends on purpose: out(...) and the values called functions return. out("note", 0, 6000) gives the message note 0 6000, out(1, 2, 3) the list 1 2 3, a str with spaces one symbol, a dict dictionary <name> (valid until the next message). bool becomes 0/1, None null; numpy numbers and arrays work. A list inside a list cannot be a Max message: send a dict.

entry.name: Log (middle outlet)
entry.description: Everything the script and its libraries print: stdout <line> and stderr <line>, a line each, as printed. Also in the Max console with console 1.

entry.name: Status (right outlet)
entry.description: pid <n> when the script starts; done <exit code> when it ends (negative: killed by that signal); error <reason> when it could not start or call found nothing running; failed <function> <message> when a call raised or named no function.

entry.name: The Python side
entry.description: A module in the package, in the Python runner's folder (py/bach_mcp/audio_processing/bachmcp_max.py, standard library only), so the runner can be driven from Max with no server running. The object does not know about it: a script imports it when it sits in the same folder (Python looks in the script's own folder first). examples/python holds a link to it for its examples. from bachmcp_max import on, out, loop. @on("name") registers a function for call (plain @on: the function's own name). out(...) sends a message at any time, from any thread (progress, streams). loop() answers calls until eof or stop. Run from a terminal instead of Max, the channel is stdin/stdout: type {"call": "transpose", "args": [6000, 200]}. Examples: examples/python/hello.py, slow.py, functions.py.

entry.name: The buffer runner
entry.description: py/bach_mcp/audio_processing/max_runner.py is the MCP server's buffer runner, driven from Max with no server: run it, then call set_playground, buffer_process_source, buffer_process_target, buffer_process_run, buffer_process_param, buffer_settings, buffer_process_stop and remove, each with the instance name first, as the server takes them. It answers with the server's own lines (<name> processing, <name> processed ..., <name> process_error ...), so a process iterates the same way with the server on or off. See the runner tab of the help.

entry.name: The channel
entry.description: JSON lines on the script's file descriptors 3 (calls in) and 4 (messages out), named in the environment variable BACHMCP_PYTHON_CHANNEL. Calls: {"call": name, "args": [...]}. Messages: {"out": [...]} and {"error": name, "message": text}. Any language can speak it; bachmcp_max is only the Python helper. Big data (audio, long arrays) is better passed by name: a shmbuffer, a dictionary, a file path.
